traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Olacaceae with Erythropalaceae, Octoknemaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins single or pinnate; stipules absent; plants hermaphrodite, monoecious or dioecious; ovary usually superior, sometimes half inferior or inferior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody; flowers in panicles, in racemes or in heads, sometimes in cymes, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, sometimes tepals; fruit drupe or nut; stamens 3 to 18; carpels (2-) 3 (-5). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Olacaceae (read 2026-10-16): leaves alternate, commonly two-ranked, or spiral. Would otherwise inherit decussate.

traits.flower_merosity.note: APweb, Santalales page (read 2026-10-16): Olacaceae flowers 3-6-merous; DELTA 3-5.

traits.fruit_type.note: Nickrent's Parasitic Plant Connection, Olacaceae description (read 2026-10-17): fruit a drupe with a leathery or crusty stone, the calyx often enlarging round it; this covers Olax, the largest genus (52 spp per Wikipedia/POWO, read 2026-10-17), with Dulacia and Ptychopetalum. A nut-like reading fits only the dry, calyx-wrapped fruits of a few small segregate genera.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Nickrent's Olacaceae description (read 2026-10-17) gives pinnate primary veins with looping secondaries and a reticulate finer net, for Olax (52 spp) and its two allied genera; a lone midrib suits only small, thick leaves.

traits.sexual_system.note: Nickrent's Olacaceae description (read 2026-10-17): flowers generally bisexual, unisexual only rarely in Olax (52 spp, the largest genus). The dioecious state comes from Octoknema, a small segregate folded in from DELTA's Octoknemaceae; monoecy is rarer still.

traits.inflorescence.note: Nickrent's Olacaceae description (read 2026-10-17): axillary racemes with cymose units, the axis zig-zag in Olax (52 spp) and Dulacia. Panicles and heads stay as lesser states from DELTA's broader family; no page read weighted them, so raceme leads only at often.
